records.reason: m146 at 2/1 and 50 uL predicts 17.13/31.86 mL. Together with the selected 5/1 row at the same loading, it tests where methylquinoline enters its late-elution regime. Measured 9e3ce3497298084abd83 gave 59.58/106.50 mL at 10/1 and 100 uL; that higher-ratio reference also changes amount.

m146 at 5/1 and 50 uL predicts 41.27/77.30 mL. The fixed-loading 2/1-to-5/1 pair distinguishes a steep transition from a gradual rise after the severe acquisition-time miss in 9e3ce3497298084abd83. Learning this boundary should inform the molecule's remaining condition rows.

m216 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 38.81/72.81 mL and directly changes mobile phase from measured 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321 at 10/1, which gave 45.80/93.07 mL. This tests whether the retrained model has placed quinoline's retention rise too early or correctly transferred its newly learned late response.

m141 at 20/1 and 150 uL predicts only 6.99/19.73 mL, below the same-loading 5/1 measurement of 16.38/46.42 mL in 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9. This tests the model's pronounced response reversal for sterically hindered aromatic nitrogen; the reversal is currently a prediction, not an observed trend.

m211 at 5/1 and 50 uL predicts 23.85/46.92 mL, extending the exactly matched 2/1 measurement of 8.14/13.44 mL in ecd17c7ea435a1e33f6b. Paired with the selected 20/1 row, it tests whether the newly elevated phenylpyridine response and its subsequent predicted decline are justified.

m211 at 20/1 and 50 uL predicts 16.76/35.05 mL, below its selected 5/1 prediction. Holding loading conditions fixed across those experiments permits a meaningful shape test. The measured 2/1 anchor ecd17c7ea435a1e33f6b prevents assuming that fused-quinoline behavior transfers uniformly to this nitrogen environment.

m160 at 2/1 and 100 uL predicts 11.09/34.93 mL. This completes a controlled ratio-by-positional-isomer comparison with measured m161 at 2/1 in 53a1acff30433cff819f and both isomers at 5/1 in b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 and 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e. It tests whether their observed difference emerges mainly near 5/1.

m72 at 5/1, 150 uL, and 200 uL DCM predicts 19.25/43.45 mL. Pairing it with 20/1 at identical loading tests transfer into a beta-enaminoester environment. Measured 2466da143763ef5563ef anchors 2/1 at 100 uL, so comparison to that anchor retains an amount difference.

m72 at 20/1 and 150 uL predicts 46.40/108.75 mL, with large single-predictor quantile widths and distant CW features. The matched 5/1 experiment tests whether this large extrapolation reflects a real response curve. Existing 2466da143763ef5563ef and a2c9096e1ec2e5c244d6 establish only stronger-eluent behavior.

First label for pyridyl ketone m66 at 5/1 predicts 10.93/24.82 mL. Its ring nitrogen plus carbonyl tests transfer between the unexpectedly late quinolines and the more modest observed pyridine-containing ester region. The label can expose a missing local nitrogen environment without presuming all aromatic bases behave alike.

Novel para-aminoester m86 at 5/1 and 150 uL predicts 11.77/23.61 mL. Measured aminobenzonitriles b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 and 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e were much later at 5/1, whereas aminoester 302e458c5ed2285ca328 was modest at 50/1. This tests functional-group and positional transfer; loading conditions differ between those references.

Meta-aminoester m88 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 10.32/20.36 mL. Measured 425074f6cad1ac0c1bc8 supplies a same-loading pure-EA anchor. This adds a weaker-eluent label for a sparsely sampled aminoester and complements m86, while their different sample amounts and loading-solvent volumes preclude a pure isomer-effect interpretation.

m28 at 5/1 and 150 uL predicts 13.25/30.16 mL. The 10/1, 50 uL measurement db7f9ffa50eb931613f6 gave 43.63/75.43 mL after a large historical underprediction. This tests whether the model correctly locates a steep response between common ratios, with the amount change explicitly remaining part of the recorded-condition contrast.

m40 at 20/1 and 100 uL predicts 17.93/30.66 mL, directly extending the same-loading 50/1 result of 38.80/67.99 mL in c2334ccf8e6788ac6ca2. The interior point constrains response curvature for an aromatic ketone whose first acquisition substantially exceeded prediction.

m164 at 20/1 and 100 uL predicts 15.76/40.83 mL. Measured c9bef93a79964dc6ede1 at 50/1 gave 28.20/68.68 mL under identical loading. This supplies a controlled solvent-response extension and an exactly matched structural comparison with the selected chalcone row.

Novel chalcone m165 at 20/1 predicts 9.53/21.65 mL. The selected m164 experiment has identical recorded conditions, allowing a direct test of the predicted conjugation-dependent difference. Measured c9bef93a79964dc6ede1 establishes late m164 behavior at 50/1 but does not establish the outcome for chalcone.

Novel acetylfluorene m38 at 20/1 predicts 18.24/37.31 mL and occupies a distant CW region. It tests fused-ring carbonyl placement beyond fluorenone evidence 486e498e45d084ced568 and acetylnaphthalene c2334ccf8e6788ac6ca2. Its 1000 uL DCM loading volume is an additional recorded difference the predictor must learn.

First label for cyclic lactone m181 at 20/1 predicts 7.81/17.34 mL. Its low similarity to observed molecules makes this a useful test of ester geometry and constrained oxygen placement beyond the acyclic ester and ketone families. A moderate prediction makes the label informative in either direction.

m195 at 50/1 and 100 uL predicts 29.78/45.64 mL. Its only measured record a917c928912c74862968 has nearly reversed endpoints, 31.98/31.91 mL, at 20/1 and 150 uL. A second condition supplies an independent retention anchor and tests naphthaldehyde versus naphthyl-ketone transfer without treating that reversed interval as mechanistic evidence.

m60 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 18.92/28.31 mL. Measured c352863d9fa4a8645481 at 10/1 gave 39.13/64.72 mL with identical loading. This directly tests whether the late secondary-alcohol regime begins sharply between 5/1 and 10/1.

Novel benzylic secondary alcohol m67 at 10/1 and 50 uL predicts 11.40/19.77 mL. It tests structural transfer after m61's unexpectedly early onset in 859ae738b615cf17b849 and the late remote-secondary-alcohol result c352863d9fa4a8645481. Loading solvent and amount differ from those references, so this is a joint structure-condition test.

m61 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 7.70/15.13 mL, directly contrasting with measured 859ae738b615cf17b849 at 10/1, 3.04/17.24 mL. This tests whether the unusually early V1 persists nearby and separates onset behavior from V2 behavior within the same alcohol.

m99 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 19.62/29.23 mL. The exactly matched 10/1 measurement c61c1a72306f2ee37df8 gave 38.99/58.03 mL, contradicting the earlier expectation of modest alpha-hydroxyester retention. This label tests response shape while retaining its 1000 uL DCM loading volume.

m205 at 2/1 and 100 uL predicts 13.63/24.23 mL, below the same-loading 1/1 result of 18.27/33.28 mL in 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8. This clean ratio contrast tests a predicted decline for a primary naphthylethyl alcohol and constrains transfer beyond the newly measured secondary-alcohol panel.

m209 at 50/1 and 150 uL predicts 20.88/55.97 mL. Measured 29b39881584c4fec1c58 at 20/1 and the same loading gave 14.43/50.83 mL. This tests whether the phenol curve flattens as predicted or grows more steeply, extending a family whose V2 was relatively stable across measured amounts.

m82 at 20/1 and 150 uL predicts 15.27/33.07 mL, below its same-loading 10/1 measurement of 18.02/40.46 mL in b6ffd4ffa7739deb3e88. This directly tests the predicted flattening or reversal against the steep measured responses of other beta-ketoesters.

m95 at 50/1 and 150 uL predicts 14.76/29.61 mL, below the same-loading 10/1 measurement of 13.30/34.07 mL in 35944fdd59ac331c3fcb for V2. Together with m82, this tests whether methyl and ethyl acetoacetate genuinely flatten while m94 and m107 show steep retention growth.

m199 at 2/1 and 50 uL predicts 10.29/20.71 mL. Measured f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c at 5/1 gave 31.09/51.75 mL under identical loading. This first controlled response extension tests whether sulfoxide retention rises sharply between 2/1 and 5/1.

m202 at 5/1 and 100 uL predicts 18.21/38.13 mL. Measured 902937db42f82f467718 at 10/1 gave 35.08/70.35 mL with identical loading. A second ratio constrains the phosphorus-containing environment's response instead of learning only an upward correction from one label; unrecorded speciation remains unknown.

Novel alpha-bromoester m76 at 50/1 and 100 uL predicts 11.12/20.07 mL. Measured methyl analogue d86448c8f5aaa8ebcf7f and less-branched bromoester b6685aed98359c179cd7 provide nearby structural anchors at different conditions. This moderate-retention test covers many eligible m76 rows and checks alkoxy-group and alpha-branching transfer.

Novel chromanealdehyde m194 at 5/1 predicts 8.06/17.02 mL and has low similarity to labeled molecules. Its cyclic ether plus aldehyde tests oxygen-placement transfer beyond methoxybenzaldehyde 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3 and the unexpectedly late acetoxybenzaldehyde db7f9ffa50eb931613f6. Those references do not isolate a causal structural effect.

First label for nitrophenethyl alcohol m200 at 2/1 and 50 uL predicts 8.79/17.98 mL. Combining a remote OH with a nitro group tests whether the graph model composes these interactions usefully. The contrasting alcohol outcomes 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48 and e4fd83fb3852eb354a66 caution against predicting this row from polarity counts alone.

hypotheses.content: Loading effects are scaffold- and endpoint-specific. Late V2 persists across measured amounts for m107, m13, m94, and m37, while V1 often changes more. Nitrobenzophenone m177 shows substantially different V2 behavior. High sample loading alone cannot explain the previous late-V2 misses.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The new contrasts weaken a loading-only explanation for broad elution intervals and support learning V1 and V2 responses separately. Several local amount questions are now sufficiently answered that response-boundary measurements have greater marginal value.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At which ratios does an amount change affect V2 as strongly as V1, and how transferable is that interaction across scaffolds? Recorded-input variability still limits causal interpretation.

hypotheses.content: Beta-ketoester solvent-response curves depend strongly on structural environment. Steep growth is measured for m94 and m107, but the current predicted flattening or reversal for methyl and ethyl acetoacetate remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Testing predicted reversals can distinguish real scaffold-specific behavior from oversmoothing and prevents imposing a universal retention increase across superficially similar carbonyl compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m82 V2 decrease between 10/1 and 20/1, and does m95 remain modest at 50/1 under fixed loading, as the current predictor suggests?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol and phenol prediction requires local structural context and scaffold-specific response curves. At sampled conditions, m60, m51, m99, and m204 are late, m61 has an unusually early onset, and m120 is more modest. The earlier low-retention expectation for m99 is weakened by its measured label.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch tests nearby ratios for observed structural contrasts and extends to a benzylic homologue and a nitro/OH combination. These labels can teach transferable local interactions rather than a global alcohol correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m60 and m99 enter their late regimes between 5/1 and 10/1? Does m61's early onset persist nearby, and does m205 actually decline between 1/1 and 2/1?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and solvent ratio jointly govern retention. Fused aromatic bases and aminobenzonitriles show late elution at their sampled ratios, while methyl anthranilate has modest retention and a measured decline from 20/1 to 50/1. Transfer to phenylpyridine, pyridyl ketones, aminoester isomers, and beta-enaminoesters remains incompletely constrained.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest recent acquisition errors identify a consequential structural failure region. Controlled response pairs and the aminobenzonitrile comparison distinguish curve location, positional effects, and overgeneralization across nitrogen classes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do quinoline responses rise, are the predicted lutidine and phenylpyridine reversals real, and does the large predicted m72 response survive direct measurement?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl attachment, conjugation, and neighboring oxygen geometry may explain the two-sided prediction failures among aromatic carbonyl compounds. Late responses in m40, m164, and m28 should transfer selectively to related structures; their causes cannot be isolated from the existing cross-molecule records alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched m164/chalcone comparison and response extensions for m40 and m28 test structural explanations for historical errors. New fused ketone, lactone, and cyclic-ether aldehyde labels cover unsupported graph environments with plausible transfer to many carbonyl rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At identical 20/1 conditions, is chalcone substantially earlier than m164? Are current curve shapes for m40 and m28 and moderate predictions for the new cyclic oxygen environments justified?

hypotheses.content: The newly observed sulfoxide and phosphorus-containing labels may mark steep retention transitions that the predictor previously missed. Their response shapes below the measured 5/1 or 10/1 anchors are still hypotheses, even though the current model now predicts higher retention.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A second condition for each functional environment distinguishes an isolated correction from a learnable structure-condition response. Fixed loading makes these extensions especially interpretable, while the phosphorus representation leaves speciation uncertain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m199 fall to approximately 21 mL V2 at 2/1 and m202 to approximately 38 mL at 5/1, or is substantial retention already present under these stronger eluents?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest outcomes strongly support environment-specific repair in nitrogen chemistry. Acquisition-time V2 errors were -90.21 mL for methylquinoline 9e3ce3497298084abd83, -74.80 mL for quinoline 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321, -54.12 mL for para-aminobenzonitrile b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90, and -46.54 mL for its meta isomer 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e. These are historical errors, not current-model residuals. Their measured late behavior now motivates testing transition locations and structural transfer. The current elevated predictions and reversals remain unverified.

The alcohol panel rejected a simple predicted ordering: m99 was much later than expected, while m61 had an unexpectedly early onset and m120 was more modest. I therefore select local response contrasts and a benzylic homologue instead of assuming OH substitution or TPSA fixes retention. Carbonyl outcomes also require two-sided learning: m40, m164, and m28 exceeded their acquisition predictions, whereas m176 and m27 were earlier than predicted.

The loading contrasts clarify the earlier failures. m107 at 50 uL still gave V2 101.44 mL versus 94.03 mL at 150 uL, and m94 V2 remained approximately 79–81 mL across all three measured amounts. m13 and m37 likewise retained late V2 while V1 shifted. This weakens an amount-only explanation for late elution. In contrast, m177 at 10/1 gave V2 20.70 mL at 100 uL versus 46.72 mL at 150 uL, preserving the need for endpoint-specific interactions. The matched m92 EA/PE pair differed by 8.56 mL in V2, supporting attention to loading-solvent identity, although its differing identical-condition records limit causal certainty.

The negative, reversed endpoints in acid record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 cannot establish rapid acid elution. I also treat the nearly reversed m195 record cautiously and acquire an independent condition anchor. No missing experimental variables or censoring convention is assumed.
batch_rationale:
The batch concentrates on relationships that remain unresolved after retraining. Nitrogen experiments have substantial value because the previous measurements exposed large errors across several related environments. The methylquinoline and phenylpyridine pairs hold loading fixed while changing ratio; the para-aminobenzonitrile selection completes a controlled positional-isomer comparison across two ratios. The m72 pair tests a large extrapolation into a different nitrogen environment, and m66/m86/m88 test whether the learned correction transfers appropriately.

Other experiments constrain response shape and structural transfer across common oxygen-containing families. The m164/chalcone pair isolates a meaningful structural change under identical recorded conditions. Alcohol, beta-ketoester, sulfoxide, and phosphorus extensions link new labels to measured anchors. Predicted decreases for m82, m95, m205, m141, and m211 receive attention because they discriminate plausible recorded non-simple behavior from model smoothing; higher PE/EA is a weaker eluent, but that prior is not imposed as an absolute endpoint rule. Amount or loading-solvent differences from an anchor are stated where present.

Exploration targets specific unsupported graph environments, including a lactone, acetylfluorene, chromanealdehyde, a benzylic alcohol homologue, and a nitro/OH combination. The moderate alpha-bromoester and several modest nitrogen/oxygen predictions provide opportunities to repair false late-retention transfer as well as underprediction. Multiple labels on a molecule serve response experiments; repeated eligible IDs with identical inputs are not duplicated within this batch. Quantile widths and CW distance provide context rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Together, the labels should improve structure-condition mapping over many remaining Row-distribution conditions without relying on a blanket upward correction.
